subject: Re: Marketplace invoicing / escrow routing — MSA addendum coordination
messages:
From: Amelia Turner <amelia.turner@cloudmarket.inc>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@cloudmarket.inc
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Marketplace invoicing / escrow routing question

Hi Marissa —

Thanks again for walking us through the partner paper last week. Legal at CloudMarket is chewing through the reseller addendum and has a couple of follow-ups before we can finalize the order form flows:

1) We need a clear routing for customer payments that flow through the marketplace. Specifically: Do invoices get issued by Redwood to the end-customer and then CloudMarket remits to Redwood, or does Redwood invoice CloudMarket and CloudMarket invoices the end-customer? Our procurement team said the pass-through language in the draft is ambiguous.

2) Escrow: for certain enterprise customers we require a short-term escrow hold for 60 days pre-reconciliation. We want to confirm whether Redwood is comfortable with an escrow account (third-party) receiving settlement funds and then Redwood pulling once monthly with a CSV reconciliation.

3) Audit & records: we need sample mappings of invoice line items and a list of evidence we can share during audits (sampling only).

Can you point us to an operational flow / contact at Redwood (ops/finance/legal) to validate? If possible, a redline showing the specific pass-through language you can accept would speed this along.

Best,
Amelia
Marketplace Ops — CloudMarket Inc.

Attachment: none
From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
To: Amelia Turner <amelia.turner@cloudmarket.inc>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 23 Jun 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketplace invoicing / escrow routing question

Hi Amelia —

Thanks for the clear list. We can do the routing either way with a preference for Redwood invoicing CloudMarket (Redwood issues consolidated invoices, CloudMarket passes payment through to us), but we can support the alternate flow if your tax/merchant setup requires CloudMarket to issue to end-customers.

Escrow: we are open to a temporary escrow arrangement. Operationally this is what we propose:
- CloudMarket remits settlement funds to third-party escrow (details in attached sample).
- Redwood pulls agreed settled funds monthly via CSV reconciliation.
- We add a 60-day reconciliation hold window for flagged invoices.

I've attached a redline of the addendum with suggested language for pass-through (redwood_marketplace-addendum_v3_redlines.docx) and a sample invoice mapping CSV (sample-invoice-mapping.csv). Please review.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Amelia/CloudMarket confirm desired invoicing principal (Redwood-issued or CloudMarket-issued) and escrow provider.
2) Internal Redwood triage (legal + finance) to confirm the redlines.
3) DocuSign routing once language is agreed.

Cc'ing Laura (legal) and Ben (finance) to confirm there are no blocking items.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Partnerships | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0124
From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Date: Tue, 23 Jun 2026 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Marketplace invoicing / escrow routing question

Laura / Ben —

Forwarding CloudMarket's note. Key asks: preferred invoice principal, willingness to support 60-day escrow hold via third party, and sample invoice mappings for audit. I attached my proposed redlines and the sample CSV.

Specific legal points I think will need sign-off:
- Pass-through clause that calls out (a) which party issues the invoice, (b) that CloudMarket acts as collection agent when it invoices the end-customer, and (c) audit & evidence scope limited to sampling and restricted to records necessary to validate settlement amounts.
- Escrow language: liability carveouts if funds are held and later reversed / chargebacks.

Ben — can you confirm the monthly pull process works operationally (we'll need an SFTP endpoint or secure API; CSV template attached). Also any concerns about revenue recognition or tax with Redwood being the principal vs. agent?

Laura — any language you want to pre-approve before I send back to Amelia? I'm aiming to keep this simple so their procurement can sign quickly.

Thanks — Marissa
From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Marketplace invoicing / escrow routing question

Marissa / Ben —

Quick take from legal after an initial pass on your redlines:

1) Invoice principal: we can accept language that allows Redwood to be the invoicing principal by default, with an alternate path where CloudMarket invoices and is explicitly the reseller (we'll add a short clause enumerating the tax/merchant responsibilities that shift to CloudMarket in that scenario). That will protect Redwood on revenue recognition and VAT/GST liabilities.

2) Escrow: acceptable with two caveats — (a) escrow must be with an approved third party (we'll supply an approved vendor list), and (b) Redwood needs an express right to pull cleared funds monthly via the reconciliation CSV. We'll add a 60-day hold window and explicit handling for chargebacks/reversals (Redwood not liable for pre-existing chargebacks discovered post-settlement unless Redwood acted negligently).

3) Audit & records: carve the audit clause down to sampling and metadata only (invoice id, gross/fees/net, customer id) and require confidentiality protections. No broad access to systems — only CSV evidence and redacted transaction receipts.

I've made in-line comments in redwood_marketplace-addendum_v3_redlines.docx and added suggested fallback text. No deal-breakers but please note: we should avoid language that forces Redwood to accept escrow funds as a guarantee of performance.

Ben — please confirm the operational endpoints (SFTP vs API) and any timing constraints for pulls. Also flag any GL/tax notes we should call out for the account team or the customer.

- Laura
General Counsel | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai
From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Marketplace invoicing / escrow routing question — proposed next steps & DocuSign

Hi Amelia —

Thanks for the patience while we reviewed. Summary of what Redwood can accept and the implementation plan:

- Invoicing: Redwood will be the default invoicing principal. If CloudMarket requires to invoice end-customers we will add the reseller principal clause in the addendum; that path shifts tax/merchant responsibility to CloudMarket and will require CloudMarket to confirm tax registrations where applicable.

- Escrow: Redwood accepts a 60-day temporary escrow model provided the escrow provider is on our approved list. Redwood will perform a monthly pull of cleared funds using the reconciliation CSV (attached sample). Chargeback handling: Redwood is not responsible for pre-existing reversals discovered after settlement unless due to Redwood negligence.

- Audit & evidence: Limited to sampling of invoice metadata and redacted receipts per the addendum language attached. No direct system access.

Attachments: redwood_marketplace-addendum_v3_redlines.docx (with comments), sample-invoice-mapping.csv, docuSign-envelope-47721.pdf (DocuSign will route to Amelia -> CloudMarket legal -> Redwood signing).

If this matches CloudMarket's expectation, please confirm the escrow provider name and we'll send the DocuSign envelope for signatures (link below):
https://www.docusign.com/envelopes/ENV-47721

Once signed we'll execute the order form onboarding checklist (ops handoff, SFTP/API details, and test settlement run).

Best regards,
